original_question: For the space-homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation in the regime gamma + 2s < 0, do global-in-time classical solutions exist? The paper identifies this very soft potential regime as unresolved even though homogeneous well posedness is understood when gamma + 2s >= 0.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at an unnumbered open problem, not a numbered conjecture: in §2.3 the paper states that for the space-homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation the well-posedness theory is well understood when γ+2s≥0, whereas the existence of global-in-time classical solutions remains open when γ+2s<0; §7 then sharpens the same issue by saying that, even in the homogeneous setting, no a priori L^∞ estimate is known in the very soft potential regime γ+2s<0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the equation (space-homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann), the parameter range (the very soft regime γ+2s<0), the precise status claimed by the paper (global-in-time classical existence is unresolved there), and the contrast with the better-understood homogeneous theory for γ+2s≥0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
missing_details: The paper is discussing the homogeneous Cauchy problem ∂_t f=Q(f,f), where f=f(t,v) is independent of x and Q is the Boltzmann collision operator from (2.2); that setup should be stated explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The collision kernel is not arbitrary: it is the standard non-cutoff inverse-power-law kernel satisfying (2.3), parameterized by γ and s with 0<s<1, and the open range is exactly the very soft potential case γ+2s<0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
The paper's open problem concerns arbitrary or generic initial data, not the perturbative near-Maxwellian regime. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The nearby context takes classical homogeneous solutions with sufficient decay as |v|→∞ and finite mass, energy, and entropy as the natural setting; your draft leaves those assumptions implicit. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-34089-5_3))

The paper's sharper formulation of the obstruction is the absence of an a priori L^∞ bound in the homogeneous very soft regime, even before asking for full global regularity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The later numbered conjectures in §7.2 are Landau-Coulomb-specific; they are not the exact Boltzmann statement, even though the paper says similar intuition may apply in the Boltzmann soft-potential case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
refined_question: For the space-homogeneous Cauchy problem ∂_t f(t,v)=Q(f,f)(t,v) on [0,∞)×R^d, where Q is the standard non-cutoff Boltzmann collision operator (2.2) with collision kernel B satisfying the inverse-power-law bounds (2.3) for some 0<s<1 and very soft parameters γ+2s<0, does every sufficiently smooth initial datum f_0(v) with sufficient decay as |v|→∞ and finite mass, energy, and entropy generate a global-in-time classical solution for arbitrary data, rather than only in a perturbative near-Maxwellian regime? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
justification: I did not replace your draft by Conjecture 7.3 or Conjecture 7.5, because those are stated specifically for the homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation. The closest paper-faithful target for the Boltzmann case is the unnumbered open problem stated in §2.3 and revisited in §7: homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann theory is understood when γ+2s≥0, but in the very soft range γ+2s<0 the existence of global classical solutions remains open, with the paper identifying the missing homogeneous L^∞ a priori estimate as the key unresolved point. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
